When it does not return there, lfs_file_flushedwrite() goes on to call lfs_bd_prog() with (`lfs`, `&file->cache`, `&lfs->rcache`) (line 3634); lfs_file_relocate() with (`lfs`, `file`) (line 3646); lfs_alloc_ckpoint() with (`lfs`) (line 3658).

results.q: What does lfs_mkdir do when the name is too long?
answer: This is handled in lfs_mkdir_() (lfs.c:2643): it checks `nlen > lfs->name_max`, and when that is true it returns `LFS_ERR_NAMETOOLONG`, so the rest of lfs_mkdir_() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: lfs_alloc_ckpoint(), lfs_dir_alloc(), lfs_dir_fetch(), lfs_pair_tole32() — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when mounting finds an unsupported on-disk version?
answer: This is handled in lfs_mount_() (lfs.c:4541): it checks `major_version != lfs_fs_disk_version_major(lfs) || minor_version > lfs_fs_disk_version_minor(lfs)`, and when that is true it records it (`err = LFS_ERR_INVAL`) and jumps to `cleanup` (line 4650), where it calls lfs_unmount_(), skipping the rest of lfs_mount_().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: lfs_fs_disk_version_minor(), lfs_fs_prepsuperblock(), lfs_min(), lfs_dir_getgstate() — the previous values stay in place.
It is computed in lfs_crc():
lfs_crc() (lfs_util.c:17) — Software CRC implementation with small lookup table.
Step by step, it sets `const uint8_t *data = buffer` (line 25); then it repeats while `i < size` (line 27); then it returns `crc` (line 32).
The result is stored in lfs_emubd_crc_.crc_ by lfs_emubd_crc_() (bd/lfs_emubd.c:557: `crc_ = lfs_crc(crc_, b->data, cfg->block_size)`).
The result is stored in lfs_emubd_crc_.crc_ by lfs_emubd_crc_() (bd/lfs_emubd.c:563: `crc_ = lfs_crc(crc_, &erase_value, 1)`).
The result is stored in lfs_emubd_bdcrc.crc_ by lfs_emubd_bdcrc() (bd/lfs_emubd.c:592: `crc_ = lfs_crc(crc_, &i_crc, sizeof(uint32_t))`).
The result is stored in lfs_bd_crc.crc by lfs_bd_crc() (lfs.c:170: `*crc = lfs_crc(*crc, &dat, diff)`).

Related values are also set here: `fcrc->crc = lfs_fromle32(fcrc->crc)` in lfs_fcrc_fromle32() (lfs.c:464); `fcrc->crc = lfs_tole32(fcrc->crc)` in lfs_fcrc_tole32() (lfs.c:470); `commit->crc = lfs_crc(commit->crc, buffer, size)` in lfs_dir_commitprog() (lfs.c:1615); `commit->crc = lfs_crc(commit->crc, &ccrc.tag, sizeof(lfs_tag_t))` in lfs_dir_commitcrc() (lfs.c:1747); `commit->crc = 0xffffffff` in lfs_dir_commitcrc() (lfs.c:1767).
The value is computed just before: `} ccrc` (lfs.c:1742).

It is called by lfs_dir_compact() at lfs.c:1996 with (`lfs`, `dir->pair[1]`), only when `tired && lfs_pair_cmp(dir->pair, (const lfs_block_t[2]){0, 1}) != 0` is false, repeatedly inside `while (true)`; lfs_ctz_extend() at lfs.c:2935 with (`lfs`, `nblock`), repeatedly inside `while (true)`, only when `err` is false; lfs_file_relocate() at lfs.c:3278 with (`lfs`, `nblock`), repeatedly inside `while (true)`, only when `err` is false.

lfs_config.prog is a field of type `int (*)(const struct lfs_config *, lfs_block_t, lfs_off_t, const void *, lfs_size_t)`, defined in lfs.h:171 — the code describes it as: "Program a region in a block. The block must have previously been erased. Negative error codes are propagated to the user. May return LFS_ERR_CORRUPT if the block should be considered bad.".
Nothing in this code assigns lfs_config.prog after its declaration.
It is read by lfs_bd_flush() (line 182), lfs_init() (line 4229).

In short: lfs_config.prog carries a value and consumed by lfs_bd_flush(), lfs_init().

results.q: Where is the read cache invalidated?
answer: It is invalidated in lfs_cache_drop():
lfs_cache_drop() (lfs.c:31) — Caching block device operations ///.
Step by step, it sets `rcache->block = LFS_BLOCK_NULL` (line 35).

Related values are also set here: `lfs->rcache.buffer = lfs->cfg->read_buffer` in lfs_init() (lfs.c:4281); `lfs->rcache.buffer = lfs_malloc(lfs->cfg->cache_size)` in lfs_init() (lfs.c:4283); `lfs->pcache.buffer = lfs->cfg->prog_buffer` in lfs_init() (lfs.c:4292); `lfs->pcache.buffer = lfs_malloc(lfs->cfg->cache_size)` in lfs_init() (lfs.c:4294); `bd->readed += size` in lfs_emubd_read() (bd/lfs_emubd.c:320); `file->cache.buffer = NULL` in lfs_file_opencfg_() (lfs.c:3087).

There is no `lfs_defragment_blocks` in this code (none of its 2843 indexed symbols has that name). The closest names are lfs_emubd.blocks (bd/lfs_emubd.h:149), lfs_fsinfo.block_count (lfs.h:320), lfs_emubd_wear() (bd/lfs_emubd.c:645), described below.
lfs_emubd.blocks is a field of type `lfs_emubd_block_t **`, defined in bd/lfs_emubd.h:149 — the code describes it as: "array of copy-on-write blocks".

It is set by lfs_emubd_create() (`bd->blocks = malloc(bd->cfg->erase_count * sizeof(lfs_emubd_block_t*))`, line 120); lfs_emubd_create() (`memset(bd->blocks, 0, bd->cfg->erase_count * sizeof(lfs_emubd_block_t*))`, line 125); lfs_emubd_powerloss() (`bd->blocks[bd->ooo_block] = lfs_emubd_incblock(bd->ooo_data)`, line 226); lfs_emubd_powerloss() (`bd->blocks[bd->ooo_block] = ooo_data`, line 257); lfs_emubd_copy() (`copy->blocks = malloc(bd->cfg->erase_count * sizeof(lfs_emubd_block_t*))`, line 713); lfs_emubd_copy() (`copy->blocks[i] = lfs_emubd_incblock(bd->blocks[i])`, line 720).
It is read by lfs_emubd_create() (line 121), lfs_emubd_destroy() (line 195), lfs_emubd_powerloss() (line 225), lfs_emubd_read() (line 301), lfs_emubd_erase() (line 443), lfs_emubd_crc_() (line 555).
Following where its value goes: lfs_emubd.blocks → lfs_emubd_powerloss() → write() — so it ultimately influences write(), which is an output (file/device write).
lfs_emubd.blocks holds a function: at run time it points to memset(); it is called by lfs_emubd_create().

In short: lfs_emubd.blocks carries a value produced by lfs_emubd_copy(), lfs_emubd_create(), lfs_emubd_powerloss() and consumed by lfs_emubd_copy(), lfs_emubd_crc_(), lfs_emubd_create(), feeding write(). lfs_emubd_copy(), lfs_emubd_create(), lfs_emubd_powerloss() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.
